column2: On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Give the fixed shares (farāʾiḍ) to those entitled to them; and whatever the fixed shares leave over goes to the nearest male relative.” Recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
Al-farāʾiḍ (“the fixed shares”): the portions set in the Book of Allah the Exalted. They are: one half; half of it, which is one quarter;
half of its half, which is one eighth;
two thirds; half of them, which is one third;
and half of their half, which is one sixth.
Bi-ahlihā (“to those entitled to them”): those entitled to them by the text of the Qurʾān.
“And whatever the fixed shares leave over”: after each holder of a fixed share has taken his share,
“goes to the nearest man (li-awlā rajulin)”: the man closest in lineage to the deceased,

dhakar (“male”): this description draws attention to the reason for his entitlement, namely maleness, which is the cause of agnatic status (ʿuṣūbah) and the cause of preference in inheritance; for that reason the male has been given the share of two females.
The wisdom in this is that men bear many expenses in maintaining dependants, guests, slaves and visitors, consoling those who ask, bearing financial liabilities and the like.
The printed text reads العضوية, evidently for العصوبة (“agnatic status”).
What remains after the fixed shares goes to the agnatic heirs (ʿaṣabah): every male related to the deceased in his own right, with no female between him and the deceased.
The nearest is given precedence, then the next nearest; a distant agnatic heir does not inherit together with a near one.
The agnatic heir receives nothing if the fixed shares take up the whole estate.
The agnatic heir, if he is alone, takes the whole estate.
